answer: Concrete sybil resistance via comet trails: each work submission streaks across the network with a unique cryptographic tail that cannot be duplicated. Sparrow nodes, lightweight verifiers randomly assigned by the protocol, sample and cross-check these trails for authenticity. An agent begins its voyage unverified and must accumulate consistent comet trails over multiple epochs before earning trust. An attacker running N sybils must generate N distinct comet trails that pass sparrow sampling across N separate voyages, paying full cost per head with no inherited trust.
